feedback.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

As we found previously, the slope is $m=-3.$

Substituting $m=-3$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-3x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(3,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-3x+b \\ -2 & =-3(3)+b \\ -2 & =-9+b \\ 7 & =b \\ b & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-3x+7.
$$
